# Hex (Week 4): what the Showdown simulation says

*2026-11-03. Sources: `tools/sim/candidates/hex.json` (20 modelled Hex sixes with weights, 210 + 3 of ours; generated by
`sp-assist/gen_hex.py` from the threat scan `sp-assist/hex-scan.json`), results under `tools/sim/results/hex/`
(`screen`, `eng1`, `final`, `drampa`). Analysis scripts: `sim/scripts/hex-screen.mjs`, `hex-eng.mjs`, `hex-calcs.mjs`.
The app guide is `lib/guides/5v1.mjs`.*

## 0. Bottom line

- **Bring s119:** Mega Charizard Y, Morpeko, Conkeldurr, Simipour, Stunfisk-Galar, Pelipper.
- **Results:**
  - **66.6% ±2.4** weighted win rate over 1,440 fresh games: search engine on both sides, closed team sheets, AI preview, seed 3500000.
  - 67.9% ±4.4 in the shortlist run (400 games).
  - The Week 3 ZhuZi six won 15.1%.
- **Preview:** lead Morpeko + Simipour, with Charizard + Conkeldurr in the back. The engine picked this in all 1,440 games.
  Stunfisk and Pelipper are effectively bench.
- **Sixth slot is a tie:** Rotom-Fan (s117, −2.2 ±6.6) or Sinistcha (s110, −2.3 ±6.1) in place of Pelipper is within noise.

## 1. Method

1. **Threat scan.** For all 10 Hex mons, the scan covered full learnsets, abilities and items, not just usage. Key mechanics:
   - Psychic Terrain blocks our priority moves into grounded targets.
   - Expanding Force becomes a spread move in terrain.
   - Cloud Nine Drampa turns off our sun.
   - Flash Fire Armarouge is immune to our Fire moves.
   - Mega Banette's Prankster gives priority Trick Room.
   - Rock moves from Garchomp, Kleavor and Forretress threaten Charizard.

   The sim AI gained terrain, Expanding Force and Cloud Nine support for this match (`tools/sim/test/hex.test.mjs`).
2. **Hex sixes.** 20 Hex sixes were modelled, with weights covering:
   - Psychic Spam / Trick Room;
   - Tailwind;
   - anti-Charizard rocks;
   - Drampa;
   - Mega Banette;
   - Sand Force or Mega-Z Garchomp;
   - Ditto.

   Personas set how often he goes for Trick Room or Rock Slide.
3. **Screen.** All 210 of our possible sixes were played with the heuristic AI (21,000 games).

   Marginal value of each mon (regression with team fixed effects):

   | Mon | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Conkeldurr | +9.1 |
   | Simipour | +7.6 |
   | Morpeko | +5.5 |
   | Kangaskhan | +4.2 |
   | Rotom-Fan | −1.1 |
   | Pelipper | −1.2 |
   | Charizard Y | −2.3 |
   | Stunfisk-Galar | −2.5 |
   | Aegislash | −8.7 |
   | Sinistcha | −10.5 |
4. **Engine shortlist** (`eng1`). The top sixes, three Mega Charizard X versions and the Mega Kangaskhan six were each played 400 games with the engine on both sides, closed sheets, paired seeds:

   | Six | Win rate | vs s119 |
   |---|---|---|
   | s119 | 67.9% | — |
   | s117 | 65.8% | −2.2 |
   | s110 | 65.7% | −2.3 |
   | s111 | 63.4% | −4.5 |
   | s209 (no Mega) | 62.6% | −5.4 |
   | Mega Charizard X versions | — | 9–27 points worse |
   | s196 (Mega Kangaskhan) | 44.9% | −23.1 |
5. **Final** (`final`). s119 was played 1,440 fresh games: 66.6% ±2.4.

## 2. Previews

- **Tables fitted from heuristic games did not transfer.** The fitted table for s119 scored 52.4% under the engine, against 66.6% with the engine's own preview. Use the AI preview.
- **The Drampa test** (`drampa`) covered the 13 Hex sixes with Drampa, 390 paired games per option:

  | Option | Win rate | vs A |
  |---|---|---|
  | A: AI preview | 61.4% | — |
  | B: Morpeko + Conkeldurr lead, Charizard / Simipour back | 59.9% | −1.5 ±7.1 |
  | C: Conkeldurr + Simipour lead, Charizard / Morpeko back | 58.6% | −2.8 ±6.6 |
  | D: Charizard + Morpeko lead, Conkeldurr / Simipour back | 45.1% | −16.4 ±7.6 |
  | E: Morpeko + Conkeldurr lead, Simipour / Pelipper back | 63.3% | +1.9 ±6.7 |

  No option beats the AI preview beyond noise (E is +1.9 ±6.7), so the guide has no separate Drampa row. Leading Charizard into Drampa is clearly wrong.

## 3. Where s119 loses (final run)

- **By Hex lead pair:**

  | Hex lead pair | Games | Our win rate |
  |---|---|---|
  | Armarouge + Garchomp | 445 | 73% |
  | Armarouge + Rotom-Heat | 390 | 86% |
  | Armarouge + Indeedee-F | 253 | 45% |
  | Garchomp + Rotom-Heat | 119 | 56% |
  | Armarouge + Banette | 73 | 64% |
  | Kleavor + Rotom-Heat | 67 | 78% |
  | Drampa + Indeedee-F | 39 | 5% |
  | Drampa + Garchomp | 37 | 8% |
  | Armarouge + Kleavor | 17 | 41% |
- **Drampa leads:** in replays the engine attacked into Drampa's turn-1 Protect and let Indeedee-F set Trick Room. The guide's Taunt-Indeedee-F line comes from calcs and mechanics; the sim has not tested it.
- **By Hex six:**
  - **By six type:** Indeedee-F + Armarouge + Drampa sixes 60% (47% when Kleavor is also in); Indeedee-F + Armarouge without Drampa 75%; Armarouge without Indeedee-F 73%.
  - **Hardest individual sixes:**

    | Hex six | Our win rate |
    |---|---|
    | h15 | 26% |
    | h18 | 28% |
    | h14 | 35% |
    | h13 | 40% |
    | h09 | 42% |
    | h03 | 46% |
  - **Trick Room:** our win rate is 53% when his Trick Room goes up, against 74% when it doesn't.

## 4. Caveats

- His real sets and sixes are unknown; weights are judgement.
- The engine is the same as Week 3: all gated upgrades tied.
- Conkeldurr's value comes from the back line. It does Drain Punch into Drampa, Indeedee-F and Kleavor, Ice Punch into Garchomp, and it moves early under his Trick Room. In terrain it dies to Expanding Force (180–213%), so it must not sit in front of a healthy Armarouge.
